text: Levan Makashvili - The European Parliament’s documents, and the European Parliament itself, have unfortunately lost their value - the only thing left is a sporting interest: will they draft a worse document than the previous one, or will we have some new development? (05.05.2026, 14:29)

This document, along with its additions, which further worsened the original, is completely detached from reality — for us and for the public, the documents of the European Parliament, and the European Parliament itself, have unfortunately lost their value, because it does not serve the agenda of cooperation and dialogue,” said Levan Makhashvili, Chairman of the Parliament’s Committee on European Integration, in response to the report on Georgia adopted by the European Parliament’s Committee on Foreign Affairs.
According to him, today’s European Parliament agenda does not align with the agenda of a better, peaceful future for Georgia-EU relations and, more broadly, for Georgia.

“What can I tell you, you also know what we would do with this resolution [I would send it to the waste paper basket] — for a simple reason: this document, along with its additions, which have made the original document even more sharply worse, is completely detached from reality. Especially in these days and weeks, it is very clear who is actually obstructing dialogue. It is precisely the European Parliament, in the form of these specific political groups, which, driven by their own narrow political agenda, are trying as much as possible to hinder dialogue. If we look at the developments of previous years, it was exactly like this: whenever there was a prospect of resetting relations, dialogue, and cooperation, the European Parliament would swim in the completely opposite direction, and today we are observing the same thing.”

“Therefore, for us and for society, the documents of the European Parliament, and the European Parliament itself, have unfortunately lost their value, because it does not serve the agenda of cooperation and dialogue. Today, the agenda of the European Parliament does not align with the agenda of a better, peaceful future for Georgia-EU relations and, more broadly, for Georgia,” said Levan Makashvili.

On the question that the European Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee is calling for sanctions against several Georgian media outlets in the adopted report, Makashvili replied that these statements and entries in this particular document are laughable.

For your information, the European Parliament’s Committee on Foreign Affairs has adopted a report on Georgia. In the European Parliament’s Committee on Foreign Affairs, the annual report on Georgia was supported by 53 Members of the European Parliament, while 14 voted against it.
